title: Which material can force mate

D0.outcome: States which bare-king mates can be forced (queen, rook, two bishops, bishop and knight) and which cannot (two knights), and why corners matter.

D1.outcome: Classifies ten material combinations as 'can force mate' or 'cannot' and gives the corner needed for bishop and knight.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, classifies the ending (including a defender's spare pawn move, queen against a single piece, rook against a minor piece) as win, draw or still playable.

D3.outcome: Explains the corner parity for bishop and knight and verifies the claim with the tablebase.

conditions: No pawns (or a defender's spare pawn move); control the four squares around the corner; bishop and knight mate only in the corner of the bishop's colour.
contrasts: Two knights against a bare king (a draw; with a defender's pawn mate can be forced).
A rook against a bishop wins; the defender sheltering in an opposite-colour corner holds.
Which wing the pieces stand on.
